thread:
maria.cs: Hey team — Acme Corp flagged that their month-end invoice total is $2,150 higher than the dashboard's month summary. Can someone sanity-check?

tom.billing: On it. Do we have invoice id and dashboard snapshot?

maria.cs: Invoice #INV-2024-11-ACME-7832. Dashboard snapshot (UTC) 2024-11-30 23:59:59 shows 123,412 embedding units and 1,230,987 generation tokens. Invoice shows 125,170 embedding units and 1,452,413 generation tokens.

vikram.ops: Those are pretty different on generation tokens — +221k. Any retention/backfill jobs or late env reprocessing that could bump counts?

ida.accounts: No manual credits or adjustments on our side. Customer says they didn't re-run any bulk jobs. They did file a support ticket.

maria.cs: Customer provided example request with timestamps: POST /v1/engines/redwood-gen-1/completions at 2024-11-30T23:45:12Z, prompt length ~1,200 chars, expected response ~3,000 tokens. They sent a batch job of ~1,800 similar calls at ~23:45-23:55 UTC.

tom.billing: Could be a split line item issue where the invoice aggregated retries or time-window crossing into next billing cycle. I'll pull meter logs for that account between 23:40 and 00:10 UTC.

billing-bot: meter-log query queued: SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) AS minute, sum(tokens) FROM meter_events WHERE account_id='acct_ACME123' AND ts BETWEEN '2024-11-30T23:30:00Z' AND '2024-12-01T00:15:00Z' GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute; (job id q_8923)

vikram.ops: While that's running, quick sanity check: any model fallback or longer-sequence truncation that would record KV-cache misses as extra tokens? Also look for duplicated ingest from retry middleware.

tom.billing: Query q_8923 results: bulk spike at 23:46-23:56 => ~220k additional generation tokens recorded, matching invoice delta. But dashboard aggregate (hourly rollup service) shows only 1,230,987. Something skipped in rollup pipeline.

ida.accounts: So meter table has the tokens, but dashboard doesn't? Could be rollup cutover or aggregation failure. Any recent deploys to stats-worker?

vikram.ops: We pushed stats-worker 2.1.8 at 2024-11-30T22:05 UTC. No alerts then. Checking worker logs...

vikram.ops: Found error trace in stats-worker logs around 23:48 UTC: "ERROR: rollup batch handler: missing partition for acct_ACME123, skipping window 2024-11-30T23:45:00Z-23:50:00Z" — looks like a partition prune bug.

maria.cs: That aligns with customer spike window. So invoice used raw meter_events (correct), dashboard missed one of the 5-minute windows during rollup.

tom.billing: Action items: 1) Recompute rollup for the missed windows and push corrected dashboard totals; 2) Issue a bill note explaining instrumentation mismatch and confirm invoice is authoritative; 3) Add temporary alert for skipped partitions.

ida.accounts: For reconciliation, customer expects line-level proof. Can we produce per-request samples for the spike? Even anonymized: timestamps, endpoint, tokens, request_id.

vikram.ops: We can export meter_events rows for acct_ACME123 for 23:40-00:10 with columns (ts, request_id, model, tokens, retry_flag). Sample export command: 

```
COPY (SELECT ts, request_id, model, tokens, metadata->>'retry' as retry_flag FROM meter_events WHERE account_id='acct_ACME123' AND ts BETWEEN '2024-11-30T23:40:00Z' AND '2024-12-01T00:10:00Z' ORDER BY ts) TO '/tmp/acme-spike.csv' CSV HEADER;
```

vikram.ops: I'll scrub PII then attach to the ticket.

maria.cs: Also customer asked whether plan tiers could have been misapplied (they were on "growth-500k" plan). Could a mid-window plan change cause different rate calculations?

tom.billing: Plan changes are applied at invoice cutover; we log plan_version_id on meter_events. I'll include plan_version_id in the export. If they changed plan at 23:50 it would still reflect in meter events, but unlikely to create token deltas — it's just pricing.

ida.accounts: Good. Once rollup recompute completes, we'll coordinate a joint message: include reconciliation CSV + explanation + ETA for dashboard fix. Customer will want a credit if they consider the dashboard canonical.

vikram.ops: Recompute started (job id rollup_recalc_447). ETA ~18m. If it succeeds we'll backfill the hourly stats table and the dashboard should reflect the +220k tokens, resolving the discrepancy.

tom.billing: If dashboard gets updated and invoice remains higher, we still need to ensure invoice is accurate. Confirming that invoice used raw meter_events and no duplicate ingestion: initial scan shows retry_flag set true for 4% of rows — expected. No automatic de-duplication is applied at billing; we bill per-meter-event.

maria.cs: Noted. Customer prefers credit rather than an invoice adjustment. Let's wait for backfill and then propose a one-time dashboard-only credit if they accept that invoice stands.

vikram.ops: rollup_recalc_447: success at 2045006820. Hourly aggregator updated. Dashboard now matches invoice totals.

ida.accounts: I'll draft the message and proposed credit language.

maria.cs: Thanks all. I'll update the customer with exported CSV and explain root cause: rollup partition prune skipped a 5-minute window during their bulk job, causing dashboard undercount. Offer optional one-time goodwill credit and show raw meter evidence. :thumbsup:

tom.billing: Filing follow-up ticket to improve partition monitoring and add a reconciliation job that compares raw meter totals to dashboard hourly aggregates at cutover. ticket: FIN-1259

maria.cs: Closing loop here. Will post customer response.
